## Overview On ROCm, `--kda-prefill-backend flashkda` is rejected at argument parsing (`--kda-prefill-backend=flashkda is only available on CUDA.`). This PR makes it run AITER's FlashKDA chunked prefill (`chunk_kimi_delta_attn`) for the GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layers on ROCm gfx950. `auto` is unchanged and stays on Triton. ## Claims - ROCm gfx950: `--kda-prefill-backend flashkda` runs GLM-5.3-Flash KDA prefill through AITER FlashKDA. AITER reads and updates the paged fp32 recurrent state in place and writes into the layer output, so the state gather, the state scatter and the merge copy are skipped. - Measured (MI355X, TP2, image+text requests): output throughput +5.6 % to +7.4 % at concurrency 16–64, TTFT −7 % to −9 %, TPOT −5 % to −7 %; the gold-answer probability check shows no change beyond noise. With breakable CUDA graphs (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`): +4.8 % to +7.3 %. - An unmet requirement is a startup error, not a silent fallback. - Unchanged: `auto` and `triton` on ROCm, all CUDA paths, and steps that carry speculative-decode tokens (they keep the Triton chunk path). Other ROCm KDA models still reject `flashkda`, now when their layer is built. ## Validation **Serving.** Speculative decoding off. - Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd` (vLLM `c50aca144`, AITER 0.1.26) with this PR's three `vllm/` files. Those three files are identical in `c50aca144` and this PR's base. - Hardware: AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), tensor parallel 2. - Model: `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, revision `b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07`. - Baseline: `--kda-prefill-backend triton`. Patched: `--kda-prefill-backend flashkda`. Otherwise the same server flags. - Benchmark: `sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm-chat`, one 512×512 image plus text per request, 1024 input / 128 output tokens (range ratio 0.8), request rate inf, 10 × concurrency prompts per level; server launches in the order baseline, patched, patched, baseline, 2 measured runs per level after a warm-up pass. ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 \ --revision b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07 \ --quantization quark --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \ --mm-processor-kwargs '{"min_image_tokens": 16, "max_image_tokens": 8000}' \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code # plus --kda-prefill-backend triton (baseline) or flashkda (patched) ``` ```bash # benchmark client, at each concurrency C in 16, 32, 64 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm-chat --port 8000 \ --model amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name image \ --image-resolution 512x512 --image-count 1 --random-input-len 1024 \ --random-output-len 128 --random-range-ratio 0.8 --seed 42 \ --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((10 * C)) --warmup-requests $((2 * C)) \ --request-rate inf ``` | Concurrency | Output tok/s baseline | Patched | Change | TTFT | TTFT p99 | TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 16 | 577.2 | 609.5 | +5.6 % | −6.8 % | −5.8 % | −5.2 % | | 32 | 769.7 | 823.1 | +6.9 % | −8.7 % | −3.9 % | −6.4 % | | 64 | 982.1 | 1054.9 | +7.4 % | −7.0 % | −5.5 % | −7.0 % | Mean change over concurrency 16–64: +6.65 %, SE 0.47 pp. SE: standard error of the change in percentage points, estimated from baseline-vs-baseline (A/A) runs with the same procedure; a change beyond about 2 SE is outside run-to-run noise. - Kernels used: in both patched launches the Triton cache holds AITER `flash_kda.py` kernels and no FLA `chunk_delta_h.py` kernels; in both baseline launches, the reverse. - Accuracy: gold-answer probability from prompt logprobs (`max_tokens=1`, so it exercises prefill) on 805 multiple-choice image items, in every launch. Patched − baseline: −0.34 pp, 95 % CI [−1.15, +0.48] pp; baseline − baseline: +0.37 pp. The smallest change this setup detects is 1.71 pp. **Serving with breakable CUDA graphs.** The same comparison (image, model, benchmark, launch order) with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` and `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", "custom_ops": ["all", "-conv2d"]}'` in both arms: | Concurrency | Output tok/s baseline | Patched | Change | TTFT | TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 16 | 613.3 | 642.5 | +4.8 % | −3.8 % | −4.6 % | | 32 | 872.3 | 923.7 | +5.9 % | −9.0 % | −5.3 % | | 64 | 1097.3 | 1177.0 | +7.3 % | −3.9 % | −7.1 % | Mean change over concurrency 16–64: +5.97 %. The two baseline launches differ by +0.3 %, −0.2 % and +4.5 % at concurrency 16, 32 and 64, so the c64 change is the least certain. Every request completed in every run. **Unit tests** (CPU host, torch 2.14.1+cpu, `--noconftest`; the GPU test also on MI355X, below): ``` $ pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_prefill_backend.py \ tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py::test_aiter_flashkda_prefill_matches_triton SKIPPED [1] tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py:438: Requires CUDA or ROCm 3 passed, 1 skipped, 1 warning in 7.58s ``` - `test_rocm_flashkda_resolves_to_aiter`: `flashkda` resolves to the AITER backend on ROCm. On the base commit, with the platform reported as ROCm, the resolver raises `RuntimeError: FlashKDA requires CUDA SM90/SM10x/SM12x, ...`. - `test_aiter_flashkda_skips_steps_with_spec_tokens`: a step with speculative-decode tokens does not reach AITER. - `test_aiter_flashkda_prefill_matches_triton` (GPU; gfx950 with AITER, skipped on CUDA) compares the layer's output and recurrent state between AITER and the Triton chunk path. On MI355X (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd` with this PR's three `vllm/` files, AITER 0.1.26, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`): passed; max abs error 9.8e-4 for the output and 6.8e-3 for the final state, tolerance 0.02. - CI: the GPU test runs only with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` on gfx950 with an AITER that has the FlashKDA paged-state API, and is skipped elsewhere; the two CPU tests run on any platform. - The GPU test reuses the layer setup of `test_prefill_checkpoint_resumes_suffix` in the same file; building the layer through its constructor would need tensor-parallel initialization and weights. ## Details - **Scope.** `Glm5NextLinearAttention` (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/kda.py`), used only by GLM-5.3-Flash, on ROCm gfx950; CUDA is unchanged. The Kimi-K3, Kimi-Linear and AliceAI KDA layers also read `--kda-prefill-backend`: on ROCm `flashkda` now passes argument parsing, and their layers reject it when built. - **Requirements**, checked at layer construction; the error lists every unmet one: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, gfx950, AITER 0.1.23 or later (paged `state_cache` and `out`), head_dim 128, bfloat16, `lower_bound` in [−5, 0), and an fp32 recurrent state (not `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16`). - **Backend name.** On ROCm the layer stores `aiter_flashkda`, so the CUDA FlashKDA code, which reserves prefix-cache checkpoint blocks, is not entered. - **Numerics.** FlashKDA uses chunk size 32 and Triton 64; outputs agree to bf16 precision, not bit for bit. - **Host read.** AITER reads `cu_seqlens` on the host to plan its chunks, so the call runs under `gpu_sync_allowed()`, as the FLA path does for its chunk indices. ROCm/aiter#6912 adds a `cu_seqlens_cpu` argument that would let a follow-up pass the host bounds instead. - **Not measured:** concurrency outside 16–64, long inputs, TP 1/4/8, speculative decoding, AITER 0.1.23 to 0.1.25. - **Related PRs** (checked 2026-10-25). None routes GLM-5.3-Flash KDA prefill to AITER. - #55737 (merged): CUDA FlashKDA for GLM-5.3-Flash; this PR gives `flashkda` a ROCm path. - #56036 (open): AITER `chunk_kimi_delta_attn` for Kimi-K3 under the same value, with the same `arg_utils.py` change. It returns the final state for the layer to scatter; this PR uses the paged `state_cache`. - #59552 (merged): `rocm_aiter_ops.kda_chunk_prefill`; the new `kda_flashkda_prefill` follows it. - Nearby edits without functional overlap: #63072 and #61614 (other branches of `kda.py`), #61951 (Triton checkpoints; `aiter_flashkda` reserves none), #61250 (FlashInfer selection in the same resolver). This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed every line and ran the tests listed. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

nodes.body:
I read the code and the AITER v0.1.26 entry points but ran nothing myself. I think the change is well contained: an opt-in backend name, `auto` unchanged, spec steps kept on the Triton path. The perf methodology is sound (same image, interleaved launches, A/A-based standard error, kernel provenance from the Triton cache). In my opinion, the existing performance/accuracy tests already justify this PR. However:

- Testing with long-context inputs would be a valuable addition because AITER may switch to a segmented recurrence once a sequence reaches 64 chunks of 32 tokens (`flash_kda.py:821-857`, `flash_kda.py:1082-1096`). The reported runs and the GPU parity test stay around 1K tokens or below. @amd-sriram's TP4 sweep covers the throughput and TTFT point, but 1) it measures more than this PR, and 2) addresses accuracy only partially: a perfect NIAH score only indicates accuracy that is above a certain threshold for both arms. What is still missing is a triton versus flashkda accuracy comparison at the maximum supported length, with a score that is less than perfect (like the logprob checks in this PR).


- One serving comparison with prefix caching left on would also be useful. A cache hit passes `has_initial_state` and the saved state slot directly to AITER (`gdn_attn.py:560-561`, `kda.py:761-764`).

`vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:2875` — With this, `flashkda` reaches every ROCm KDA layer. The shared Kimi GDN layer rejects it only by `assert` (`kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py:285`), so under `python -O` the flag is ignored and the Triton kernel runs. Turning that check into `raise ValueError` would keep the rejection. The Kimi-K3 path still raises later, making the issue more cosmetic. (PR #56036 also touches this hunk for Kimi-K3.)

On MI355X (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd` with this PR's three `vllm/` files, AITER 0.1.26, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`): passed; max abs error 9.8e-4 for the output and 6.8e-3 for the final state, tolerance 0.02. - CI: the GPU test runs only with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` on gfx950 with an AITER that has the FlashKDA paged-state API, and is skipped elsewhere; the two CPU tests run on any platform. - The GPU test reuses the layer setup of `test_prefill_checkpoint_resumes_suffix` in the same file; building the layer through its constructor would need tensor-parallel initialization and weights. ## Details - **Scope.** `Glm5NextLinearAttention` (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/kda.py`), used only by GLM-5.3-Flash, on ROCm gfx950; CUDA is unchanged. The Kimi-K3, Kimi-Linear and AliceAI KDA layers also read `--kda-prefill-backend`: on ROCm `flashkda` now passes argument parsing, and their layers reject it when built. - **Requirements**, checked at layer construction; the error lists every unmet one: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, gfx950, AITER 0.1.23 or later (paged `state_cache` and `out`), head_dim 128, bfloat16, `lower_bound` in [−5, 0), and an fp32 recurrent state (not `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16`). - **Backend name.** On ROCm the layer stores `aiter_flashkda`, so the CUDA FlashKDA code, which reserves prefix-cache checkpoint blocks, is not entered. - **Numerics.** FlashKDA uses chunk size 32 and Triton 64; outputs agree to bf16 precision, not bit for bit. - **Host read.** AITER reads `cu_seqlens` on the host to plan its chunks, so the call runs under `gpu_sync_allowed()`, as the FLA path does for its chunk indices. ROCm/aiter#6912 adds a `cu_seqlens_cpu` argument that would let a follow-up pass the host bounds instead. - **Not measured:** concurrency outside 16–64, long inputs, TP 1/4/8, speculative decoding, AITER 0.1.23 to 0.1.25. - **Related PRs** (checked 2026-10-25). None routes GLM-5.3-Flash KDA prefill to AITER. - #55737 (merged): CUDA FlashKDA for GLM-5.3-Flash; this PR gives `flashkda` a ROCm path. - #56036 (open): AITER `chunk_kimi_delta_attn` for Kimi-K3 under the same value, with the same `arg_utils.py` change. It returns the final state for the layer to scatter; this PR uses the paged `state_cache`. - #59552 (merged): `rocm_aiter_ops.kda_chunk_prefill`; the new `kda_flashkda_prefill` follows it. - Nearby edits without functional overlap: #63072 and #61614 (other branches of `kda.py`), #61951 (Triton checkpoints; `aiter_flashkda` reserves none), #61250 (FlashInfer selection in the same resolver). This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed every line and ran the tests listed. ---

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GLM-5.3-Flash KDA prefill through AITER FlashKDA on ROCm. Nothing here
+needs a GPU: the platform and the AITER probe are faked."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+from vllm.models.glm5next.common import kda
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import GDNAttentionMetadata
+
+
+def test_rocm_flashkda_resolves_to_aiter(monkeypatch):
+    """``--kda-prefill-backend flashkda`` selects AITER FlashKDA on ROCm
+    instead of being rejected."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(kda.current_platform, "is_rocm", lambda: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        rocm_aiter_ops, "is_kda_flashkda_prefill_available", lambda: True
+    )
+    backend = kda._resolve_kda_prefill_backend(
+        "flashkda",
+        head_dim=128,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        lower_bound=-5.0,
+        state_dtype=torch.float32,
+    )
+    assert backend == "aiter_flashkda"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("num_spec_decodes", "expected"), [(0, True), (1, False)], ids=["no-spec", "spec"]
+)
+def test_aiter_flashkda_skips_steps_with_spec_tokens(num_spec_decodes, expected):
+    """Steps that carry speculative-decode tokens keep the Triton chunk path."""
+    spec_tokens = 4 * num_spec_decodes
+    metadata = GDNAttentionMetadata(
+        num_prefills=2,
+        num_prefill_tokens=74,
+        num_decodes=0,
+        num_decode_tokens=0,
+        num_spec_decodes=num_spec_decodes,
+        num_spec_decode_tokens=spec_tokens,
+        num_actual_tokens=74 + spec_tokens,
+        spec_sequence_masks=(
+            torch.tensor([True] * num_spec_decodes + [False] * 2)
+            if num_spec_decodes
+            else None
+        ),
+    )
+    assert kda._aiter_flashkda_runs_prefill("aiter_flashkda", metadata) is expected

@@ -284,7 +284,10 @@ def test_prefill_checkpoint_resumes_suffix(monkeypatch, dim_first, num_spec, off
     from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import compute_causal_conv1d_metadata
     from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import WorkspaceManager
 
-    if kda._resolve_kda_prefill_backend("auto", D, torch.bfloat16, -5) != "flashkda":
+    if (
+        kda._resolve_kda_prefill_backend("auto", D, torch.bfloat16, -5, torch.float32)
+        != "flashkda"

         pytest.skip("requires FlashKDA")
     import vllm._flashkda_C  # noqa: F401

         actual[:, : length - offset], expected[:, suffix], atol=0.003, rtol=0.03
     )
     torch.testing.assert_close(recurrent[3], expected_state, atol=0.003, rtol=0.03)
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_aiter_flashkda_prefill_matches_triton(monkeypatch):
+    """With ``flashkda`` on ROCm the layer's prefill runs AITER FlashKDA on
+    the paged state and output in place, and matches the Triton chunk path
+    to bf16 precision (chunk size 32 vs 64)."""
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.common import kda
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import GDNAttentionMetadata
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import compute_causal_conv1d_metadata
+
+    if not rocm_aiter_ops.is_kda_flashkda_prefill_available():
+        pytest.skip("requires AITER FlashKDA (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1, gfx950)")
+
+    torch.manual_seed(7)
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    # 32 local heads: the default 64 KDA heads at tensor parallel size 2.
+    heads, lengths = 32, [37, 100]
+    num_tokens, num_slots = sum(lengths), 4
+    width, state_len, slot_size = 3 * heads * D, 3, heads * D * D
+    layer = object.__new__(kda.Glm5NextLinearAttention)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(layer)
+    layer.prefix = "layer.0"
+    layer.local_num_heads = heads
+    layer.head_dim = D
+    layer.local_projection_size = heads * D
+    layer.kda_safe_gate = True
+    layer.kda_lower_bound = LOWER_BOUND
+    layer._conv_state_dim_first = False
+    layer.conv1d = SimpleNamespace(
+        weight=0.5 * torch.randn(width, 1, 4, device=device), bias=None
+    )
+    layer.A_log = 0.5 * torch.randn(1, 1, heads, 1, device=device)
+    layer.dt_bias = 0.1 * torch.randn(heads * D, device=device)
+
+    # Padded slot strides, as in the hybrid KV cache.
+    conv_storage = torch.randn(
+        num_slots, width * state_len + 8, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    recurrent_storage = 0.5 * torch.randn(num_slots, slot_size + 8, device=device)
+    projected = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, width + heads, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    raw_qkv, beta = projected[:, :width], projected[:, width:].unsqueeze(0)
+    gate = torch.randn(1, num_tokens, heads, D, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    cu_cpu = torch.tensor([0, lengths[0], num_tokens], dtype=torch.int32)
+    nums, batch_ptr, chunk_offsets = compute_causal_conv1d_metadata(
+        cu_cpu, device=device
+    )
+    metadata = GDNAttentionMetadata(
+        num_prefills=len(lengths),
+        num_prefill_tokens=num_tokens,
+        num_decodes=0,
+        num_decode_tokens=0,
+        num_spec_decodes=0,
+        num_spec_decode_tokens=0,
+        num_actual_tokens=num_tokens,
+        has_initial_state=torch.tensor([True, False], device=device),
+        non_spec_query_start_loc=cu_cpu.to(device),
+        non_spec_state_indices_tensor=torch.tensor(
+            [1, 2], dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        ),
+        nums_dict=nums,
+        batch_ptr=batch_ptr,
+        token_chunk_offset_ptr=chunk_offsets,
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        kda,
+        "get_forward_context",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(attn_metadata={layer.prefix: metadata}),
+    )
+
+    prefill_calls = []
+    kda_flashkda_prefill = rocm_aiter_ops.kda_flashkda_prefill
+
+    def spy(**kwargs):
+        prefill_calls.append(kwargs)
+        return kda_flashkda_prefill(**kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rocm_aiter_ops, "kda_flashkda_prefill", staticmethod(spy))
+
+    def run(backend: str):
+        conv_pool, recurrent_pool = conv_storage.clone(), recurrent_storage.clone()
+        conv = conv_pool[:, : width * state_len].view(num_slots, state_len, width)
+        recurrent = recurrent_pool[:, :slot_size].view(num_slots, heads, D, D)
+        layer.kv_cache = (conv, recurrent)
+        layer.kda_prefill_backend = backend
+        out = torch.full(
+            (1, num_tokens, heads, D), float("nan"), device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        layer._forward(raw_qkv, gate, beta, out)
+        return out, recurrent
+
+    triton_out, triton_recurrent = run("triton")
+    assert not prefill_calls
+    out, recurrent = run("aiter_flashkda")
+    assert len(prefill_calls) == 1
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, triton_out, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(recurrent, triton_recurrent, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+    written = slice(1, 3)
+    for actual, expected in (
+        (out, triton_out),
+        (recurrent[written], triton_recurrent[written]),
+    ):
+        actual, expected = actual.float(), expected.float()
+        error = (actual - expected).norm() / expected.norm()
+        assert error < 2e-2, f"relative L2 error {error:.2e}"

+    @staticmethod
+    def kda_flashkda_prefill(
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        k: torch.Tensor,
+        v: torch.Tensor,
+        g: torch.Tensor,
+        beta: torch.Tensor,
+        A_log: torch.Tensor,
+        dt_bias: torch.Tensor,
+        lower_bound: float,
+        cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+        state_cache: torch.Tensor,
+        state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+        has_initial_state: torch.Tensor,
+        out: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Run AITER FlashKDA chunked prefill over a paged recurrent state.
+
+        ``q``, ``k`` and ``v`` are ``[1, T, H, 128]`` bf16, ``g`` is the raw
+        gate of the same shape and ``beta`` the raw ``[1, T, H]`` logits; the
+        gate activation and the sigmoid run in the kernel. ``A_log`` is
+        ``[H]`` and ``dt_bias`` ``[H * 128]``, both fp32. ``state_cache`` is the
+        fp32 V-first ``[slots, H, V, K]`` pool: sequence ``n`` reads and writes
+        row ``state_indices[n]`` in place. ``out`` must be contiguous with
+        ``v``'s shape. Returns ``out``.
+        """
+        from aiter.ops.triton.kimi_delta_attn import chunk_kimi_delta_attn
+
+        logger.info_once("Dispatching AITER FlashKDA KDA prefill.")
+        # AITER reads cu_seqlens on the host to plan its chunks and segments.
+        with gpu_sync_allowed():
+            chunk_kimi_delta_attn(
+                q=q,
+                k=k,
+                v=v,
+                g=g,
+                beta=beta,
+                A_log=A_log,
+                dt_bias=dt_bias,
+                use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+                use_gate_in_kernel=True,
+                use_beta_sigmoid_in_kernel=True,
+                safe_gate=True,
+                lower_bound=lower_bound,
+                state_v_first=True,
+                # 32 selects the FlashKDA kernels, the only ones that take
+                # state_cache and out.
+                chunk_size=32,
+                cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+                out=out,
+                state_cache=state_cache,
+                state_indices=state_indices,
+                has_initial_state=has_initial_state,
+            )
+        return out
+

reviews.body:
Nice, well-evidenced change: same-image A/B with an A/A standard error, a kernel-provenance check and a prefill logprob check. I read the new branch against the Triton one: the guards, the spec-step fallback, the zero checkpoint blocks and the in-place state all line up. The host read is cached per step, just like the Triton path's prepare_chunk_indices. Few suggestions:
1. The GPU parity test never runs in CI (inline comment).
2. Modify the test to include longer sequence length case (inline comment). 
3. Please cite @amd-sriram's TP4 long-context and NIAH 64k results in Validation, noting they ran with #63612 and AITER main rather than v0.1.26.

I read the code and the AITER v0.1.26 entry points but ran nothing myself. I think the change is well contained: an opt-in backend name, `auto` unchanged, spec steps kept on the Triton path. The perf methodology is sound (same image, interleaved launches, A/A-based standard error, kernel provenance from the Triton cache). In my opinion, the existing performance/accuracy tests already justify this PR. However:

- Testing with long-context inputs would be a valuable addition because AITER may switch to a segmented recurrence once a sequence reaches 64 chunks of 32 tokens (`flash_kda.py:821-857`, `flash_kda.py:1082-1096`). The reported runs and the GPU parity test stay around 1K tokens or below. @amd-sriram's TP4 sweep covers the throughput and TTFT point, but 1) it measures more than this PR, and 2) addresses accuracy only partially: a perfect NIAH score only indicates accuracy that is above a certain threshold for both arms. What is still missing is a triton versus flashkda accuracy comparison at the maximum supported length, with a score that is less than perfect (like the logprob checks in this PR).


- One serving comparison with prefix caching left on would also be useful. A cache hit passes `has_initial_state` and the saved state slot directly to AITER (`gdn_attn.py:560-561`, `kda.py:761-764`).

`vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:2875` — With this, `flashkda` reaches every ROCm KDA layer. The shared Kimi GDN layer rejects it only by `assert` (`kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py:285`), so under `python -O` the flag is ignored and the Triton kernel runs. Turning that check into `raise ValueError` would keep the rejection. The Kimi-K3 path still raises later, making the issue more cosmetic. (PR #56036 also touches this hunk for Kimi-K3.)
